item.title: Edge-structure fault diameters of exchanged hypercubes
item.description: arXiv:2611.00764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the edge-structure and edge-substructure fault diameters of the exchanged hypercube $EH(s,t)$ for every $1\le s\le t$. Both parameters equal $s+t+4$, two more than the fault-free diameter, except for $EH(2,2)$, where both are nine, and $EH(1,1)$, where they are five and six, respectively. This holds even though an admissible family may remove up to $2s$ vertices, more than the vertex connectivity $s+1$. For every $s\ge2$, the maximum is attained by $s$ parallel fault edges in class $0$. For $s\ge3$, the structure-fault diameter exceeds the classical $s$-vertex-fault diameter by exactly one.
item.dc:creator: Lihui Dong, Zhuo Li

item.title: Mutual-visibility colouring with two colours is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.01012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A mutual-visibility set in a graph $G$ is a set $S$ of vertices such that any two vertices of $S$ are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition $V(G)$. Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter $d$, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. The proof rests on a reformulation of $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the $2$-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from $2$-colourability of $3$-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.
item.dc:creator: Siddhesh Chaubal

item.title: Two-Dimensional Search for a Moving Target on Rectangular and Cylindrical Grids
item.description: arXiv:2611.01281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how precisely a moving target can be localized on finite rectangular grids and their cylindrical counterparts. Each query asks whether the target lies in a chosen subset of vertices and receives a noiseless answer. Queries may depend on previous answers. Between successive queries, the target may stay in place or move along one horizontal or vertical edge. Accuracy is measured by the number of positions still possible immediately after the final answer, with no subsequent movement. A strategy achieves accuracy $s$ if it always terminates with at most $s$ possible positions, whatever admissible trajectory the target follows. Thus $s=1$ means exact localization. We denote by $s^*(M,N)$ the smallest value of $s$ achievable by a finite adaptive strategy on a finite grid. Our main result shows that every finite rectangular grid admits a strategy that localizes the target to at most eight positions, regardless of the grid dimensions: $s^*(M,N)\leq8$. The construction uses nine local query patterns and their vertical reflections. Its termination follows from the progress these patterns force toward the finite grid boundaries. We also prove the dimension-dependent bound $s^*(M,N)\leq\min\{M+1,N+1\}$. For finite cylindrical grids $P_M\square C_N$, where the columns are periodic but the first and last rows remain boundaries, we introduce the corresponding accuracy parameter and state the proposed dimension-independent bound $s^*_{\mathrm{cyl}}(M,N)\leq9$.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Lebedev, Vladimir Lebedev, Christian Deppe

item.title: Metric Testing: A Characterization of One-Sided Testability
item.description: arXiv:2611.01346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a unified framework for one-sided testability (constant-query testing) of metric families. For a broad class of families defined by fixed local predicates, we prove that testability is equivalent to two structural properties: \emph{packing amplification}, which turns many edge-disjoint local violations into a positive density of violations, and \emph{completion stability}, which allows locally consistent partial matrices with few missing entries to be cheaply completed. This characterization yields a common proof strategy and simpler proofs of classical testability results for ultrametrics, tree pseudometrics, Euclidean pseudometrics in fixed dimension, and several others. Our framework also gives new quantitative bounds for metric testing: a nonadaptive one-sided upper bound for matrices with entries in the bounded range $[1,C]$, and two-sided nonadaptive and adaptive lower bounds for general metrics.
item.dc:creator: Zihan Tan, Theo Teske

item.title: Searching the Plane in the Segment Visibility Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.03161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study deterministic search by $n \geq 2$ unit-speed robots starting at the origin of the Euclidean plane. We introduce the concept of \emph{segment visibility} whereby a stationary target $x$ at distance $d=\|x\|>0$ is discovered at the first instant $t$ when $x$ belongs to the segment joining a pair of robots at time $t$. Discovery time is compared with the omniscient optimum $d$. We distinguish two knowledge models according to whether the robots know $d$ in advance. For $n=2$ robots, in the \emph{known-$d$} model, we give a symmetric four-phase algorithm and prove that its competitive ratio is optimal: $1+\sqrt3+\pi/6$; the matching lower bound follows from the known-distance two-robot shoreline-search theorem through an explicit reduction to segment detection. For $n=2$ robots, in the \emph{unknown-$d$} model, a three-circle construction and a quantitative initial-path estimate yield the stronger lower bound $\sqrt3+\pi/6+\sqrt{17}/4 \approx3.286425990$, giving an explicit positive cost for not knowing the radius; we also analyze a feasible antipodal-diameter logarithmic-spiral algorithm with optimized ratio $8.928516954\ldots$, thus proving that the competitive ratio when $d$ is unknown is at least $ \sqrt3+\pi/6+\sqrt{17}/4 $ and at most $8.928516954\ldots.$ For $n \geq 3$ robots, the competitive ratio of finding the target is exactly $\sec (\pi/n)$ regardless of whether or not $d$ is known to the robots.
item.dc:creator: Evangelos Kranakis

item.title: An Almost-tight Size Lower Bound for Bounded Treewidth Homomorphism-Distinguishability
item.description: arXiv:2611.03579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One way to compare two graphs $G_1, G_2$ is to check whether there is some graph $H$ in a graph class $\mathcal{H}$, such that the number of homomorphisms from $H$ to $G_1$ is not equal to that from $H$ to $G_2$. This is the field of homomorphism distinguishability which has gained a lot of traction in recent years. In this paper, we study the case where $\mathcal{H}$ is the class of graphs of treewidth $k$. This has connections to important concepts in logic, machine learning, combinatorial optimization and proof complexity. In particular, Dvo\v{r}\'ak showed that $G_1$ and $G_2$ can be distinguished by a homomorphism count from a graph of treewidth $k$ iff $G_1$ and $G_2$ are distinguishable by the $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm. While the relation between the iteration number of this algorithm and the depth of the tree-decomposition of a distinguishing graph is understood, our understanding of the \emph{size} of $H$ is limited. We show a $2^{\Omega(n^{k/2})}$ lower bound on the size of a graph of treewidth $k$ required to distinguish two graphs of order $n$. This bound is proved via a new combinatorial game along with a construction which uses a recent compression technique for CFI graphs. It is almost tight to the known $2^{O(n^{k+1})}$ upper bound and is an exponential improvement on the previous best known lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Lichter, Harry Vinall-Smeeth

item.title: The symbolic pfaffian method I: A generalization of the Gallucio-Loebl-Tesler Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.00468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The pfaffian number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\mathrm{pf}(G)$, is the minimum integer $k$ such that the generating function of perfect matchings of $G$ can be written as a linear combination of $k$ pfaffians of signed adjacency matrices. The Galluccio-Loebl-Tesler Theorem states that $\mathrm{pf}(G) \leq 4^g$, where $g$ is the orientable genus of $G$. We generalize this theorem by relating the pfaffian number of a graph to another graph parameter: the symbolic pfaffian number, denoted by $\mathrm{spf}(G)$. Namely, we prove that $\mathrm{pf}(G) \leq 2^{\mathrm{spf}(G)}$. Our proof is based on linear algebra arguments and does not depend on topological properties of graphs. As a consequence of our generalization, we conclude that $\mathrm{pf}(K_{2n}) = 2^{\mathcal{O}(n \log n)}$, an improvement on the previous upper bound of $4^{\mathcal{O}(n^2)}$ based on the genus. We also consider lower bounds for $\mathrm{pf}(G)$ related to $\mathrm{spf}(G)$. In particular, we show that the graphs with $\mathrm{pf}(G) = 4$ are the graphs with $\mathrm{spf}(G) = 2$. On the other hand, we show that our main result is strictly more general than a previous generalization by Norine.
item.dc:creator: Enrique Junchaya, Cl\'audio L. Lucchesi, Alberto A. A. Miranda

item.title: $K_h$-Minor-Free Graphs Have Balanced Separators of Size $O(h\sqrt{n})$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that every $K_h$-minor-free graph with $n$ vertices has a balanced separator of size $O(h\sqrt{n})$ for any parameter $h \in \mathbb{N}$, resolving the conjecture posed by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [AST90] in 1990. The proof is elementary, building on the combinatorial framework by Le [Le26]. A key new idea of the proof is the existence of a short hitting walk on vertex expanders: given $k$ large (not necessarily disjoint) subsets of vertices, there is a walk of length $O(k/\psi(G))$ hitting every subset, where $\psi(G)$ is the vertex expansion. This technical result substantially improves on an analogous lemma by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [AST90] in an important parameter setting, where the previous lower bound [Kot00] does not apply.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Conroy, Hung Le, Jack Spalding-Jamieson

item.title: Claw-free perfect graphs are chromatic-choosable
item.description: arXiv:2611.01068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every claw-free perfect graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=\chi(G)=\omega(G)$. More strongly, if $S$ is a clique of simplicial vertices of $G$ and $k\ge\omega(G)$, every proper precoloring of $S$ extends to a proper coloring of $G$ from arbitrary lists of size $k$ on $V(G)\setminus S$. The proof has three coloring steps: a mixed-list theorem for cobipartite graphs, a precoloring-extension theorem for elementary graphs built on Galvin's kernel method and a homogeneous-pair exchange argument, and a polynomial method (Combinatorial Nullstellensatz) argument for graphs of interval type in which a Vandermonde factor is transferred across each incomplete pair. The three coloring steps are assembled along the structure theorems of Chv\'atal--Sbihi, Maffray--Reed and Chudnovsky--Seymour, using double clique cutsets for composition. As a consequence, every perfect line graph is chromatic-choosable, recovering the theorem of Peterson and Woodall. Our precoloring extension theorem also resolves a conjecture posed by Chudnovsky and Seymour.
item.dc:creator: Suchismita Mishra, Narayanan Narayanan, Umesh Shankar

item.title: The Value of Steiner Hubs in Two-Hop Distance Labeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two-hop distance labelings were introduced in 2002 by Cohen, Halperin, Kaplan, and Zwick with hubs of two kinds: vertices of the graph, or, in their Steiner variant, arbitrary objects carrying arbitrary real values. On no family is the value of that freedom known. We determine it on $\ell_1$ products of betweenness-free metrics, those with no point between two others, a class containing every Hamming graph. The freedom is worth nothing when the factors have at most three letters, while from four letters on the largest saving is polynomial in the size of the product, attained on products of positively weighted stars. The $d$-dimensional hypercube is the two-letter case, and labeling it takes $(5/2+o(1))^d$ entries even with arbitrary hubs, matching the vertex-hub optimum of Goldberg, Razenshteyn, and Savchenko. Every lower bound here comes from one semidefinite program on a single factor, whose value $\Lambda$ never exceeds the rate that vertex hubs already achieve on the Hamming graph; where $\Lambda$ meets that ceiling, the freedom is worth nothing, and the ceiling is met exactly up to three letters.
item.dc:creator: Sichen Wang

item.title: Entropic Column Generation and Lehmer Branch-and-Price for Bin Packing Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Lehmer branch-and-price, an exact algorithm for bin packing and cutting stock problems built on the Lehmer transform, the ratio of Mellin transforms of item weights at consecutive orders. The transform maps each bin, a finite multiset of item weights, to a smooth increasing curve, and so gives the discrete problem a continuous representation on which the tools of analysis, such as convexity, exponential families and smoothing, can act. Read along this curve, the problem yields an explicit dual solution, a monotone representation of the dominance order, a family of constructive heuristics with first fit decreasing as its limit, and an integer identity that tells when the linear relaxation can decide an instance and when only a perfect packing can improve the best solution known. Lifted from items to patterns, the transform gives entropic column generation, a new form of column generation that bounds the relaxation from both sides at every iteration without solving the pricing problem exactly, maximizes a smoothed dual at an explicit rate, and measures by an entropy how much the relaxation leaves undecided. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the standard benchmark in both the number of instances solved and the computational time.
item.dc:creator: Masoud Ataei

item.title: Clique counts under degree and matching constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.01259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the maximum number of $t$-cliques in graphs with maximum degree at most $D$ and matching number at most $M$, with no restriction on the number of vertices. For $t\ge 3$, we determine this maximum whenever $D\ge 2M-1$ and characterize all extremal graphs when the maximum is positive. Up to isolated vertices, these are complete or complete split graphs for $D\ge 2M$, while $K_{2M}$ is uniquely extremal when $D=2M-1$. We also derive a general upper bound from the Chv\'atal-Hanson edge theorem and refine it for even $D$. For fixed even $D$ and $3\le t\le D+1$, every extremal graph consists, apart from isolated vertices, of copies of $K_{D+1}$ together with a remainder whose order is bounded independently of $M$. When $D/2$ divides $M$, this remainder is empty and the extremal graph is unique. This structure yields an eventual recurrence, reducing the determination of all extremal values and graphs to finitely many matching bounds.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Adak

item.title: Threshold existence for random NAE-$k$-SAT and random hypergraph $2$-colourability
item.description: arXiv:2611.01338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The existence of limiting threshold densities for random hypergraph $2$-colourability and random NAE-$k$-SAT was conjectured in earlier work, including Achlioptas and Moore [RANDOM 2002] and Coja-Oghlan and Panagiotou [STOC 2012]. We prove these conjectures for all $k\geq 3$. We also show that $\alpha^{\mathrm{2-col}}_k \leq \alpha^{\mathrm{NAE}}_k$ for each $k\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Zakharov

item.title: An approximate cactus-decomposition for vertex-connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.01772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical cactus theorem of Dinitz, Karzanov and Lomonosov from 1976 states that the minimum edge-cuts of a connected graph are displayed by a cactus. For vertex-separations, Tutte's theorem gives an exact cactus-decomposition for connectivity $2$, but exact cactus-decompositions fail for higher connectivity. Extending earlier approximate cactus-decomposition results for connectivities $3$ and $4$ by Carmesin and Kurkofka [FOCS 2023] and Kurkofka and Planken [SODA 2026] to all connectivities, we prove that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is a constant $d=d(k)$ such that every $k$-connected graph $G$ admits a cactus-decomposition displaying $k$-separations such that every $k$-separation of $G$ has edit-distance at most $d$ to a displayed separation. Our proof develops tools that may be useful beyond this result. The first is a three-dimensional version of the classical corner-diagram method, which we use to show that triples of crossing $k$-separations have a controlled two-dimensional behaviour. The second is a covering-space approach for studying local crossing patterns from a global perspective. Third, we advance the theory of flowers, which originated in matroid theory.
item.dc:creator: Romain Bourneuf, Johannes Carmesin, Jan Kurkofka, Tim Planken

item.title: Monotone Local Search with Sample-Dependent Running Times
item.description: arXiv:2611.01774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monotone Local Search turns an algorithm that extends a given partial solution into an algorithm that finds a solution from scratch: sample a few elements, hope that they lie in an unknown solution, and complete them. Its known analyses bound every call of the extension algorithm by a worst-case time that depends only on the number of sampled elements, and Esmer et al. (SODA 2024) showed that no algorithm that uses the extension algorithm as a black box with this running time beats the original form by more than a polynomial factor. We let this running time depend on the actual sample. If the extension algorithm decides in time $O^*(2^{g(I,X,k)})$, for a polynomial-time computable $g$, whether a sample $X$ can be completed to a solution with at most $k$ elements, our main theorem gives a randomized algorithm with one-sided error in time $O^*(2^{\psi n})$ whenever, for some solution $S$ of size $k$ and some $t$, the exponential moment $\sum_{X\subseteq S,|X|=t}2^{-g(I,X,k)}$ is at least $2^{-\psi n}\binom{n}{t}$. A corollary, multivariate Monotone Local Search, generalizes the theorems of Fomin et al. (STOC 2016, J. ACM 2019) and of Gaspers and Lee (ICALP 2017). For Max Leaf Spanning Tree and, equivalently, Connected Dominating Set, the previous best polynomial-space bound is $O^*(1.8619^n)$. Completing a sample is a Steiner tree problem, solved in time exponential in the number of terminals, which varies strongly with the sample. We obtain a randomized polynomial-space algorithm in time $O(1.6991^n)$ and a deterministic one in time $(\sqrt5-\frac12)^n 2^{o(n)}=O(1.7361^n)$. For connectivity problems in which the extension algorithm's running time doubles with every component of the sample, an analysis through a partition function gives randomized polynomial-space algorithms in time $O^*(1.8^n)$ for Connected Feedback Vertex Set and $O(1.6444^n)$ for Connected Vertex Cover.
item.dc:creator: Serge Gaspers

item.title: Integral saturation of adjacency-degree lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.01838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of $G\sim G(n,1/2)$, let $D=\operatorname{diag}(A\mathbf{1})$, and let $\Lambda_G=\mathbb{Z}\langle A,D\rangle\mathbf{1}$. We prove $\Pr[\Lambda_G\ne\mathbb{Z}^n]\le n^{-3/20+o(1)}$. Thus two dependent graph operators generate the entire vertex lattice from the constant vector, simultaneously over every prime field. Adjacency alone has a modulo-two rank obstruction for every simple graph of order greater than one, even though its rational word span is typically full. The proof first constructs words containing at most two adjacency operations whose integer span contains $\Delta_G^3\mathbb{Z}^n$, where $\Delta_G$ is the product of the pairwise differences between distinct degree values. This confines all possible arithmetic obstructions to a finite prime range on a single event. We then remove the remaining obstructions using conditional alternating forms, symmetric random-matrix code estimates, and uniform counts of degree-graded invariant subspaces. We connect the integer lattice to graph reconstruction through pointed moments. Saturation forces every pointed orthogonal AD intertwiner to be a vertex permutation. The short-word construction also shows that a fixed polynomial-size family of ordinary caterpillars, of diameter at most seven and order $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$, identifies almost every graph among all finite simple graphs. For nonsaturated full-rank lattices, we give an exact description of the moment fibre by admissible unimodular overlattices; at index two, the only possible ambiguity is a specified four-vertex Godsil--McKay switch.
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Lu

item.title: Asymptotically Optimal Weighted Edge Colorings via Local Bin Packing
item.description: arXiv:2611.03190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weighted edge coloring, where each edge of a graph $G$ has a weight in $(0,1]$, and colors are assigned so that the incident weight of each color at every vertex is at most one. The objective is to minimize the number of colors, denoted by $\chi'_w(G)$. This generalizes classical edge coloring (all weights are one) and bin packing ($G$ is a star). Two natural lower bounds are the maximum weighted degree $\Delta_w(G)$ and the maximum local bin-packing number $\mathrm{bp}(G)$: the maximum, over vertices, of the minimum number of unit bins needed to pack the incident weights. We have $\lceil\Delta_w(G)\rceil\le\mathrm{bp}(G)\le\chi'_w(G)$. How closely these local lower bounds approximate the global optimum is a longstanding open problem. Our main result establishes an asymptotic weighted analogue of Vizing's theorem: every simple graph admits a coloring using at most $(1+o(1))\mathrm{bp}(G)$ colors. Thus local bin packings can be made globally consistent with asymptotically vanishing relative loss, even in nonbipartite graphs. Our local-to-global rounding framework coordinates feasible local packing distributions into a partial coloring, leaving only $o(\mathrm{bp}(G))$ uncolored weight at every vertex. For bipartite multigraphs, we prove $\chi'_w(G)\le(2+o(1))\Delta_w(G)$, establishing the Chung--Ross conjecture [SICOMP'91] asymptotically. For loopless multigraphs, we obtain the exact bound $\chi'_w(G)\le3\lceil\Delta_w(G)\rceil$. Both leading coefficients are optimal, giving weighted analogues of the classical K\H{o}nig--Shannon bounds. Further upper and lower bounds show that the classical factor-$3/2$ separation does not persist with the local bin-packing benchmark. We also disprove the exact weighted-degree conjecture of Feige and Singh [ESA'08]. Our upper bounds have polynomial-time algorithms, and their existence statements are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Rishikesh Gajjala, Arindam Khan

item.title: Exact Agreement Expansion up to the Top via Non-polarity
item.description: arXiv:2611.03261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agreement expansion asks whether local assignments to faces of a poset that usually agree on a sampled common face must agree with a single global function on most faces. Agreement expansion is exact (approximate) if local assignments need to exactly (approximately) agree with the global function. We suggest a new proof technique for agreement expansion that enables agreement expansion in settings which were previously beyond reach, such as: exact agreement expansion for Grassmannian posets (before only simplicial complexes support exact agreement expansion); agreement expansion based on assignments to top faces of the a complex (before agreement expansion is generally proven only for assignments to low dimensional faces); agreement expansion from one-sided spectral expansion (before, two sided spectral assumption was needed in general settings). Specifically, for down-closed simplicial and Grassmannian complexes, we prove an exact agreement theorem between any two layers assuming one-sided spectral expansion in links of singletons. As an application, we show that full bases of every rank-$k$ matroid admit exact agreement with soundness $O(k^2/[h(k-h)])$ when tested through $h$-element independent sets. We also obtain exact agreement on Grassmannian posets under one-sided spectral expansion, with stronger soundness under a local distance guarantee. Our key proof ideas center around non-polarity of the distributions of local assignments, probed via a random exposure of elements.
item.dc:creator: Tali Kaufman, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: The Optimizer's Windfall: Bounding Hindsight Gain under Random Restrictions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Suppose an optimization problem is randomly restricted, independently on each variable, and re-optimized after the restriction is revealed. For multilinear objectives, every fixed solution is unbiased after rescaling, but re-optimizing introduces an upward bias. We bound this excess, the hindsight gain, over products of arbitrary compact local domains in Euclidean unit balls. For interactions $A=(A_e)_e$ among $r$ distinct variables and independent random weights $\zeta_i$, the gain is at most $O_r(\|A\|_F M^{(r-1)/2}\sigma_{\max})$, where $\|A\|_F^2$ is the sum of squared coefficients, $M=\sum_i\mathbb{E}\zeta_i^2$, and $\sigma_{\max}^2=\max_i\mathrm{Var}(\zeta_i)$; only second moments are needed. Under uniform retention with probability $p$, we sharpen this to $O_r(p^{r-1/2}\sqrt{1-p}\,n^{(r-1)/2}\|A\|_F)$, which is tight for every fixed $r$ and $p\in(0,1)$. Our proof combines a comparison principle along a single support direction with tensor projection, vector contraction, and repeated thinning. Applications: (i) For fixed arity and alphabet size, solving the subproblem induced by $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ sampled variables estimates a dense Max-$r$CSP optimum within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, and this sample size is optimal. (ii) The same approach estimates MaxCut and the distance to bipartiteness within $\pm\varepsilon n^2$ using $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ nonadaptive queries and $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ examined vertices, both optimal. (iii) We answer a question of Yufei Zhao: vertex percolation at rate $p$ preserves the max-cut fraction whenever $p\,e(G)/v(G)\to\infty$, and this condition is sharp. (iv) For bounded $r$-local quantum Hamiltonians of fixed local dimension, $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ uniformly sampled particles suffice to estimate the ground-state energy within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, improving the previous $O(\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bound.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohui Bei, Wenhao Wu

item.title: Adjacency Labeling Schemes of Size $\log n+O(\log\log^* n)$ for Graphs of Bounded Treewidth
item.description: arXiv:2611.03620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gavoille and Labourel (ESA 2007) gave an adjacency labeling scheme of size $\log n+O(k\log\log n)$ for graphs of treewidth at most $k$, and asked whether $\log n+O(k)$ bits suffice. We give a labeling scheme of size $\log n+O(\log\log^* n)$ for every fixed $k$, the first improvement of the second-order term for any $k\ge 2$. Equivalently, there is an induced-universal graph with $n(\log^* n)^{O_k(1)}$ vertices for this family. We work with laminar families of intervals, in which a vertex finds each earlier neighbor as the owner of an interval of a given nesting depth around it. As long as every subtree occupies consecutive positions, the nesting depth must be logarithmic, and $\log\log n$ bits per neighbor follow. We give up contiguity. Heavy subtrees are moved out, which brings the depth down to $O(\log^* n)$; the intervals broken by the moves are repaired with $2^{O(k^3)}$ additional intervals per vertex; and the bits needed to find these intervals are paid for by the moved subtrees.
item.dc:creator: Noy Rotbart

item.title: On the distribution of $A_\alpha$-eigenvalues in terms of graph invariants
item.description: arXiv:2510.06933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and $A(G)$ and $D(G)$ its adjacency and degree diagonal matrices, respectively. For a parameter $\alpha \in [0,1]$, Nikiforov~(2017) introduced the convex combination $A_{\alpha}(G) = \alpha D(G) + (1 - \alpha)A(G)$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral distribution of $A_\alpha(G)$-eigenvalues, over subintervals of the real line. We establish lower and upper bounds on the number of such eigenvalues in terms of structural parameters of $G$, including the number of pendant and quasi-pendant vertices, the domination number, the matching number, and the edge covering number. Additionally, we exhibit families of graphs for which these bounds are attained. Several of our results extend known spectral bounds on the eigenvalue distributions of both the adjacency and the signless Laplacian matrices.
item.dc:creator: Uilton Cesar Peres Junior, Carla Silva Oliveira, Andr\'e Ebling Brondan

item.title: $k$-path graphs: experiments and conjectures about algebraic connectivity and $\alpha$-index
item.description: arXiv:2511.21524v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents conjectures about eigenvalues of matrices associated with $k$-path graphs, the algebraic connectivity, defined as the second smallest eigenvalue of the Laplacian matrix, and the $\alpha$-index, as the largest eigenvalue of the $A_{\alpha}$-matrix. For this purpose, a process based on [Discrete Applied Mathematics 164 (2014) 297-303] is presented to generate lists of $k$-path graphs containing all non-isomorphic 2-paths, 3-paths, and 4-paths of order $n$, for $6 \leq n \leq 26, 8 \leq n \leq 19$, and $10 \leq n \leq 18$, respectively. Using these lists, exhaustive searches for extremal graphs of fixed order for the mentioned eigenvalues were performed. Based on the empirical results, conjectures are suggested about the structure of extremal $k$-path graphs for these eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Rafael L. de Paula, Claudia M. Justel, Carla S. Oliveira, Milena S. Carauba

item.title: Structural and Spectral Properties of Strictly Interval Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2512.01175v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we deal with a subclass of chordal graphs, which are simultaneously strictly chordal and interval, the strictly interval graphs. We present a new characterization of the class that leads to a simple linear recognition algorithm. Next we introduce a new subclass of strictly interval graphs, the $SI$-core graphs, that are non-split and non-cograph graphs and show that several elements of the new class are Laplacian integral
item.dc:creator: Claudia Justel, Lilian Markenzon

item.title: A Quaternary Legendre Pair of Length 64
item.description: arXiv:2609.25573v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A quaternary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ is a pair of sequences over $\{\pm 1, \pm \mathrm{i}\}$ whose periodic autocorrelations sum to $-2$ at every nonzero shift. We give a quaternary Legendre pair of length $64$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported construction at this length.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Verma

item.title: A New Upper Bound for 7-Universal Tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2610.06891v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A tournament is $k$-universal if it contains every tournament on $k$ vertices as a subtournament. We give a 7-universal tournament on 14 vertices, improving the upper bound of 15 due to Zhang and Szeider. Together with their lower bound, it follows that the smallest 7-universal tournament has 13 or 14 vertices.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Verma

item.title: Arboricity games: the core and the nucleolus
item.description: arXiv:2010.08936v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The arboricity of a graph is the minimum number of forests required to cover all its edges. In this paper, we examine arboricity from a game-theoretic perspective and investigate cost-sharing in the minimum forest cover problem. We introduce the arboricity game as a cooperative cost game defined on a graph. The players are edges, and the cost of each coalition is the arboricity of the subgraph induced by the coalition. We study properties of the core and propose an efficient algorithm for computing the nucleolus when the core is not empty. In order to compute the nucleolus in the core, we introduce the prime partition which is built on the lattice of maximum-density edge sets. The prime partition decomposes the edge set of a graph into a non-prime set and a partially ordered collection of prime sets defined from minimal densest minors and their invariant precedence relation. Moreover, edges from the same set of the partition always have the same value in a core allocation. Consequently, when the core is not empty, the prime partition significantly reduces the number of variables and constraints required in the linear programs of Maschler's scheme and allows us to compute the nucleolus in polynomial time. Besides, the prime partition provides a graph decomposition analogous to the celebrated core decomposition and the density-friendly decomposition, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Han Xiao, Qizhi Fang

item.title: Tight (Double) Exponential Bounds for Identification Problems: Locating-Dominating Set and Test Cover
item.description: arXiv:2402.08346v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate fine-grained algorithmic aspects for classical identification problems in graphs, namely LOCATING-DOMINATING SET, and in set systems, namely TEST COVER. In the first problem, an input is a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and an integer $k$, and the objective is to decide whether there is a subset $S$ of $k$ vertices such that any two distinct vertices not in $S$ are dominated by distinct subsets of $S$. In the second problem, an input is a set $U$ of items, a collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $U$ called tests, and an integer $k$, and the objective is to select a set $S$ of at most $k$ tests such that any two distinct items are contained in a distinct subset of tests of $S$. For our first result, we show that LOCATING-DOMINATING SET (respectively, TEST COVER) parameterized by the treewidth of the input graph (respectively, the incidence graph) does not admit an algorithm running in time $2^{2^{o(\textsf{tw})}} \cdot {\rm poly}(n)$ (respectively, $2^{2^{o(\textsf{tw})}} \cdot {\rm poly}(|U| + |\mathcal{F}|)$), unless the ETH fails. Next, we prove that, unless the ETH fails, LOCATING-DOMINATING SET does not admit an algorithm running in time $2^{o(k^2)} \cdot {\rm poly}(n)$, nor a polynomial-time kernelization algorithm that reduces the solution size and outputs a kernel with $2^{o(k)}$ vertices, and TEST COVER does not admit an algorithm running in time $2^{2^{o(k)}} \cdot {\rm poly}(|U| + |\mathcal{F}|)$ nor a kernel with $2^{2^{o(k)}}$ vertices. Again, we show that these lower bounds are tight by designing (kernelization) algorithms with matching running times.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics, Vol. 40(3), 2026
item.dc:creator: Dipayan Chakraborty, Florent Foucaud, Diptapriyo Majumdar, Prafullkumar Tale

item.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2411.00721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Tron Omland

item.title: Satisfying sequences for rainbow partite matchings
item.description: arXiv:2502.03105v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal F_1,\ldots, \mathcal F_s\subset [n]^k$ be a collection of $s$ families. In this paper, we address the following question: for which sequences $f_1,\ldots, f_s$ do the conditions $|\mathcal F_i|>f_i$ imply that the families contain a rainbow matching, that is, there are pairwise disjoint $F_1\in \mathcal F_1,\ldots, F_s\in \mathcal F_s$? We call such sequences {\em satisfying}. Kiselev and the first author showed that $f_1 = \ldots = f_s=(s-1)n^{k-1}$ is satisfying for $s>470$, verifying the conjecture by Aharoni and Howard. This is the best possible if we insist that the families are of the same size. However, it turns out that much more can be said about asymmetric restrictions. In this paper, we investigate this question in several regimes and in particular answer the questions asked by Kiselev and Kupavskii. We use a variety of methods, including concentration and anticoncentration results, spread approximations, and the Combinatorial Nullstellenzatz.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Kupavskii, Elizaveta Popova

item.title: Planar induced paths via a decomposition into non-crossing ordered graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.17835v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In any graph, the maximum size of an induced path is bounded by the maximum size of a path. However, in the general case, one cannot find a converse bound, even up to an arbitrary function, as evidenced by the case of cliques. Galvin, Rival and Sands proved in 1982 that, when restricted to weakly sparse graphs, such a converse property actually holds. In this paper, we consider the maximal function $f$ such that any planar graph (and in general, any graph of bounded genus) containing a path on $n$ vertices contains an induced path of size $f(n)$, and prove that $f(n) \in \Theta (\log n/\log \log n)$ by providing a lower bound matching the upper bound obtained by Esperet, Lemoine and Maffray, up to a constant factor. We obtain these tight bounds by analyzing graphs ordered along a Hamiltonian path that admit an edge partition into a bounded number of sets without crossing edges. In particular, we prove that the guaranteed size of an induced path when the ordered graph can be partitioned into $2k$, resp. $2k+1$, sets of non-crossing edges, is $\Theta_k((\log n/\log \log n)^{1/k})$, resp. $\Theta_k((\log n)^{1/(k + 1)})$.
item.dc:creator: Julien Duron, Hugo Jacob

item.title: Making Every Number from 1 to N Under a Fixed Cycle of $+$, $\times$, $-$, $\div$
item.description: arXiv:2610.10095v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Start with the number $2$. At each move, combine two numbers already made, but the operations must be used in the fixed repeating order $+,\times,-,\div$. We ask for the fewest moves needed to make every integer from $1$ to $N$. Since $2$ is already one of the numbers we want and each move makes at most one new number, at least $N-1$ moves are needed. We show that $N-1$ moves are also enough for every $N\ge 9$. Conventional induction cannot work, because a division that comes right after a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ produces numbers already made. Instead we extend a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ to $\{1,\dots,3P\}$ all at once, which counting shows is the smallest multiplicative extension $P\to kP$ that can work, and then adjust the last few moves to reach every other $N$. For $9\le N\le 33$ we give explicit sequences, found by computer search.
item.dc:creator: Sean Lesmana, Theodore Tjugiarto

item.title: Fast Almost-Uniform Sampling of Random $k$-SAT Solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.10474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study approximately uniform sampling of satisfying assignments from random $k$-SAT formulas. Fix a constant $B>0$. For every $k\ge 2^{20}$ and density $0<\alpha\le 2^k/k^{16}$, we prove that, with high probability over a random formula on $n$ variables, every accuracy $n^{-B}\le\varepsilon\le 1/2$ admits a sampler whose output distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution on satisfying assignments with expected running time $$\widetilde O_B\left(\mathrm{poly}(k,\alpha+1)n^{2+\eta}\right),\quad 0<\eta\le 2^{16-k}.$$ In particular, the exponent of $n$ is $2+O(2^{-k})$ while the dependence on the width and density is polynomial with a universal degree. This improves the parameter-dependent polynomial exponent of the sampling algorithm of Chen, Lonkar, Wang, Yang, and Yin (STOC 2025) in the density regime $2^k/\mathrm{poly}(k)$. Our algorithm separates a high-degree core from the remaining variables. Every residual formula on the good variables is a deletion subformula of a common bounded-dependency formula. Adapting the rejection--repair framework of Liu, Wang, Yin, Zhang and Zhou (arXiv 2026), we construct an executable sampler for all such residual formulas using ordinary connected violation sets replacing weighted 2-tree witnesses and use it to simulate approximate block heat-bath updates on the core. To analyze the resulting core chain, we integrate out the good variables, represent the core marginal by an absolutely convergent polymer expansion and combine a component-swap variance comparison with an adaptive exploration bound. Absorbing single-component interactions into the local weights leaves interactions of cluster size at least two; retaining their additional decay gives a spectral gap of at least $1/(2s n^{2^{12-k}})$ where $s$ counts core components. Together with the residual sampler, this yields the stated running time.
item.dc:creator: Kun He, Zhidan Li, Kuan Yang

item.title: Rapid Mixing for Sampling Colorings of Random Graphs up to Tree Uniqueness Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.25391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the mixing time of the single-site Glauber dynamics for sampling proper $q$-colorings on sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$. We prove that, whenever $q \ge (1 + o_d(1))d$, Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time with high probability over $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. This improves the previous bound $q = (\alpha^* + o_d(1))d$ where $\alpha^* = 1.7632...$ is the unique solution of $x = \exp(1/x)$ on $[1, \infty)$ by Efthymiou, Hayes, \v{S}tefankovi\v{c}, and Vigoda (SODA, 2018) and asymptotically matches the uniqueness threshold on infinite regular trees. Our proof has three main ingredients. First we establish logarithmic bounds on the spectral and coupling independence constants of the Gibbs distribution by extending the tree analysis of Chen, Liu, Mani, and Moitra (J. ACM, 2026). Second, we extend the entropy-factorization framework for two-spin systems on random graphs, developed by Bez\'akov\'a, Galanis, Goldberg, and \v{S}tefankovi\v{c} (TALG, 2024), to proper colorings by introducing a buffer around high-degree vertices. Finally, we compare the resulting heat-bath block dynamics with the single-site Glauber dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Zhidan Li, Kuan Yang

item.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
item.description: arXiv:2610.34556v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $\eta_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{\eta_i,\eta_j\in S:\eta_i\neq\eta_j}|\mathcal N(\eta_i-\eta_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Shiu
